title_en: Labor Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated in accordance with the Constitution to protect the lawful rights and interests of laborers, regulate labor relations, establish and maintain a labor system suited to the socialist market economy, and promote economic development and social progress.

Article 2 This Law shall apply to enterprises and individual economic organizations (hereinafter collectively referred to as "employing units") within the territory of the People's Republic of China and to laborers who form labor relations therewith.
State organs, institutional organizations, and social organizations and the laborers with whom they conclude labor contracts shall implement this Law.

Article 3 Laborers shall have the right to equal employment and choice of occupation, the right to obtain labor remuneration, the right to rest and leave, the right to obtain labor safety and health protection, the right to receive vocational skills training, the right to enjoy social insurance and welfare, the right to submit labor disputes for handling, and other labor rights provided for by law.
Laborers shall complete their labor tasks, improve their vocational skills, implement labor safety and health regulations, and observe labor discipline and professional ethics.
Article 4 Employing units shall, according to law, establish and perfect rules and regulations to ensure that laborers enjoy labor rights and perform labor obligations.

Article 5 The State shall adopt various measures to promote employment, develop vocational education, formulate labor standards, regulate social income, improve social insurance, coordinate labor relations, and gradually raise the living standards of laborers.

Article 6 The State shall encourage laborers to participate in social voluntary labor, launch labor emulation and rationalization proposal campaigns, encourage and protect laborers in engaging in scientific research, technological innovation, and inventions, and commend and reward model laborers and advanced workers.

Article 7 Laborers shall have the right to participate in and organize trade unions according to law.
Trade unions shall represent and safeguard the lawful rights and interests of laborers and shall carry out their activities independently and autonomously according to law.

Article 8 In accordance with the provisions of the law, laborers shall, through a general meeting of the staff and workers, a congress of the staff and workers, or other forms, participate in democratic management or conduct equal consultations with employing units on the protection of the lawful rights and interests of laborers.

Article 9 The labor administrative department of the State Council shall be in charge of the labor work nationwide.
The labor administrative departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall be in charge of the labor work within their respective administrative areas.

Article 10 The State shall create employment conditions and expand employment opportunities by promoting economic and social development.
The State shall encourage enterprises, institutional organizations, and social organizations to establish industries or expand operations within the scope provided for by laws and administrative regulations to increase employment.
The State shall support laborers in voluntarily organizing themselves for employment and in undertaking self-employment to realize employment.
Article 11 Local people's governments at all levels shall adopt measures to develop various types of employment placement agencies and provide employment services.
Article 12 In employment, discrimination based on ethnicity, race, gender, or religious belief shall not be practiced against laborers.

Article 13 Women shall enjoy equal employment rights with men. In the recruitment of staff and workers, no employer may refuse to recruit women or raise the recruitment standards for women on the grounds of gender, except for the types of work or positions that are unsuitable for women as prescribed by the State.
Article 14 Where laws and regulations have special provisions on the employment of disabled persons, persons of minority ethnic groups, and discharged servicemen, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 15 Employing units shall be prohibited from recruiting minors under the age of 16.
Units of literature and art, sports, and special crafts that recruit minors under the age of 16 must comply with the relevant provisions of the State and guarantee their right to receive compulsory education.

Article 16 A labor contract is an agreement for establishing a labor relationship between a laborer and an employing unit and for specifying the rights and obligations of the parties thereto.
A labor contract shall be concluded when a labor relationship is established.

Article 17 The conclusion and modification of a labor contract shall follow the principles of equality, voluntariness, and consensus through consultation, and shall not violate the provisions of the law or administrative regulations.
A labor contract concluded according to law shall have legal binding force from the time it is concluded. The parties must perform the obligations stipulated in the labor contract.

Article 18 The following labor contracts shall be void:
(1) Those that violate the provisions of the law or administrative regulations;
(2) Those concluded by means of fraud, duress, or the like.
A void labor contract shall have no legal binding force from the time of its conclusion. Where a part of a labor contract is determined to be void and does not affect the validity of the remaining parts, the remaining parts shall remain valid.
The invalidity of a labor contract shall be determined by a labor dispute arbitration committee or a People's Court.

Article 20 The term of a labor contract shall be divided into a fixed term, an indefinite term, and a term based on the completion of a specific task.
Where a laborer has been continuously working in the same employing unit for not less than ten years and the parties agree to extend the labor contract, if the laborer proposes to conclude a labor contract with an indefinite term, an indefinite term labor contract shall be concluded.
Article 21 A labor contract may provide for a probation period. The probation period shall not exceed six months.
Article 22 The parties to a labor contract may agree in the labor contract on matters concerning the protection of the employer's trade secrets.

Article 23 Upon the expiration of a labor contract or the occurrence of the conditions for the termination of the labor contract agreed upon by the parties, the labor contract shall terminate immediately.
Article 24 A labor contract may be rescinded if the parties to the labor contract have reached a consensus through consultation.

Article 27 Where an employer is on the verge of bankruptcy and undergoing statutory reorganization, or experiences serious difficulties in production and business operations, and indeed needs to reduce its workforce, it shall explain the situation to the trade union or all of its employees 30 days in advance, solicit the opinions of the trade union or the employees, and may reduce the workforce after reporting to the labor administrative department.
Where the employer reduces its workforce in accordance with this Article and recruits personnel within six months, it shall give priority to the re-employment of the persons so laid off.

Article 28 Where the employer rescinds the labor contract in accordance with the provisions of Articles 24, 26 and 27 of this Law, it shall provide economic compensation in accordance with the relevant regulations of the State.

Article 30 Where the trade union considers it inappropriate for the employer to rescind a labor contract, it shall have the right to put forward its opinions. If the employer violates laws, regulations or the labor contract, the trade union shall have the right to require a reconsideration. Where a worker applies for arbitration or initiates a lawsuit, the trade union shall provide support and assistance according to law.
Article 31 A worker who intends to rescind the labor contract shall notify the employer in writing 30 days in advance.

Article 33 The employees of an enterprise may conclude a collective contract with the enterprise regarding matters such as labor remuneration, working hours, rest and vacation, occupational safety and health, insurance and welfare. The draft collective contract shall be submitted to the workers' congress or all the employees for discussion and adoption.
A collective contract shall be concluded between the trade union representing the employees and the enterprise on behalf of the employees; in an enterprise where a trade union has not been established, such a contract shall be concluded between the representatives elected by the employees and the enterprise.

Article 34 A collective contract shall be submitted to the labor administrative department after its conclusion; if the labor administrative department raises no objections within 15 days from the date of receipt of the text of the collective contract, the collective contract shall take effect automatically.

Article 35 A collective contract concluded according to law shall be binding on the enterprise and all its employees. The standards regarding working conditions and labor remuneration in the labor contracts concluded between individual employees and the enterprise shall not be lower than those provided in the collective contract.
Article 36 The State adopts a working hours system under which workers shall work no more than eight hours a day and no more than an average of 44 hours per week.

Article 37 For workers engaged on a piecework basis, the employer shall rationally determine the work quotas and the piecework remuneration rates in accordance with the working hours system provided for in Article 36 of this Law.
Article 38 The employer shall guarantee that its workers have at least one day off per week.

Article 39 Where an enterprise is unable to implement the provisions of Articles 36 and 38 of this Law due to the nature of its production, it may, with the approval of the labor administrative department, adopt other measures for working hours and rest.

Article 41 If an employer needs to extend working hours due to its production or business operations, it may do so after consulting with the trade union and the workers, provided that the extended hours shall not exceed one hour per day in general. Where the extension of working hours is needed for special reasons, under the condition that the health of workers is guaranteed, the extended hours shall not exceed three hours per day, but shall not exceed thirty-six hours per month.
Article 43 An employer shall not extend the working hours of workers in violation of the provisions of this Law.

Article 45 The State shall implement a system of annual leave with pay.
Workers who have worked continuously for one year or more shall be entitled to annual leave with pay. The specific measures shall be formulated by the State Council.

Article 46 The distribution of wages shall follow the principle of distribution according to work and equal pay for equal work.
Wage levels shall be gradually increased on the basis of economic development. The State shall exercise macro-control over the total amount of wages.

Article 47 An employer shall, according to its own production and business characteristics and economic results, independently determine its own wage distribution method and wage level in accordance with law.

Article 48 The State shall implement a minimum wage guarantee system. The specific standards of minimum wage shall be prescribed by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and shall be reported to the State Council for the record.
An employer shall not pay its workers a wage lower than the local minimum wage standard.
Article 50 Wages shall be paid to the workers themselves in monetary form on a monthly basis. No deduction or unjustified delay of payment of wages shall be made.

Article 51 An employer shall pay wages to workers in accordance with law during statutory holidays, marriage or funeral leaves and during the period when they participate in social activities in accordance with law.

Article 52 An employer must establish and perfect the labor safety and health system, strictly implement the national rules and standards for labor safety and health, provide education to workers on labor safety and health, prevent accidents in the process of labor, and reduce occupational hazards.

Article 53 The labor safety and health facilities must conform to the standards prescribed by the State.
The labor safety and health facilities for newly built, rebuilt or expanded projects must be designed, constructed and put into production and use simultaneously with the main projects.

Article 54 An employer must provide workers with labor safety and health conditions conforming to the provisions of the State and necessary labor protection articles. For workers engaged in operations with occupational hazards, the employer shall conduct regular health examinations.
Article 55 Workers engaged in special operations must receive specialized training and obtain qualifications for such special operations.

Article 56 Workers must strictly observe safety operation procedures in the process of labor.
Workers shall have the right to refuse to carry out orders from the management personnel of the employer that are in violation of rules and compel risky operations, and shall have the right to criticize, report and file charges against acts that endanger life safety and health.

Article 57 The State shall establish a system of statistics, reporting and handling of casualties and occupational diseases. The labor administrative departments of the people's governments at or above the county level, relevant departments and employers shall, in accordance with law, carry out statistics, reporting and handling of the casualties and occupational diseases of workers that occur in the process of labor.

Article 58 The State shall provide special labor protection to female workers and minor workers.
A minor worker refers to a worker who has reached the age of 16 but not the age of 18.

Article 59 It shall be prohibited to arrange female workers to engage in underground mining work, work with Grade IV physical labor intensity as prescribed by the State, or other work that is forbidden for them.

Article 60 No female workers shall be arranged to engage in work at heights, in low temperatures, in cold water, or work with Grade III physical labor intensity as prescribed by the State during their menstrual periods.

Article 61 No female worker shall be assigned to work at Grade III physical labor intensity as prescribed by the State or other work forbidden for female workers during their pregnancy. Female workers who are pregnant for more than seven months shall not be assigned to overtime work or night shift work.
Article 62 A female worker shall enjoy maternity leave of not less than 90 days for childbirth.

Article 63 No female worker shall be assigned to work at Grade III physical labor intensity as prescribed by the State or other work forbidden for nursing mothers during the period of nursing her baby under one year old. She shall not be assigned to overtime work or night shift work.

Article 64 No juvenile worker shall be assigned to underground work in mines, work which is toxic or harmful, work at Grade IV physical labor intensity as prescribed by the State, or other work forbidden for them.
Article 65 An employing unit shall conduct regular physical examinations for juvenile workers.

Article 66 The State shall develop vocational training programs through various channels and by various measures, in order to develop the vocational skills of workers, improve their qualifications, and enhance their employment and work capabilities.

Article 67 The people's governments at all levels shall incorporate the development of vocational training into their plans for social and economic development, and encourage and support enterprises, institutions, social organizations and individuals with the necessary conditions to provide various forms of vocational training.

Article 68 An employing unit shall establish a vocational training system, withdraw and use vocational training funds in accordance with State regulations, and provide vocational training to workers in a planned manner according to the actual conditions of the unit.
Workers engaged in technical jobs must receive training before taking up their posts.

Article 69 The State shall determine occupational classifications, formulate vocational skill standards for the specified professions, and implement a vocational qualification certificate system. The examination and assessment bodies that have been put on record shall be responsible for carrying out vocational skill examination and assessment of workers.

Article 70 The State shall develop social insurance undertakings, establish a social insurance system, and set up a social insurance fund, so that workers may receive assistance and compensation under such circumstances as old age, illness, work-related injury, unemployment, and childbirth.
Article 71 The level of social insurance shall be commensurate with the level of social and economic development and the social capacity to bear.

Article 72 The source of funds for social insurance funds shall be determined according to the type of insurance, and the pooling of social insurance funds shall be gradually carried out. Employing units and workers must participate in social insurance and pay social insurance premiums according to law.

Article 74 The social insurance fund agencies shall, in accordance with legal provisions, receive, manage, and operate the social insurance funds, and bear the responsibility of maintaining and increasing the value of the social insurance funds.
The social insurance fund supervision agencies shall, in accordance with legal provisions, exercise supervision over the receipt, management, and operation of the social insurance funds.
The establishment and functions of the social insurance fund agencies and the social insurance fund supervision agencies shall be prescribed by law.
No organization or individual may misappropriate the social insurance funds.

Article 75 The State shall encourage employing units to establish supplementary insurance for workers according to their actual conditions.
The State shall encourage individual workers to take out savings-type insurance.

Article 76 The State shall develop social welfare undertakings, construct public welfare facilities, and provide conditions for workers to rest, recuperate and convalesce.
Employing units shall create conditions to improve collective welfare and raise the welfare benefits of workers.

Article 77 Where a labor dispute arises between an employing unit and a worker, the parties may apply for mediation, arbitration, bring a lawsuit, or resolve the dispute through consultation according to law.
The principle of mediation shall apply to arbitration and legal proceedings.

Article 78 The resolution of a labor dispute shall be based on the principles of lawfulness, fairness, and timeliness, and shall protect the legitimate rights and interests of the parties to the labor dispute according to law.

Article 79 After the occurrence of a labor dispute, the parties may apply to the labor dispute mediation committee of their unit for mediation; if mediation is unsuccessful, and one of the parties requests arbitration, that party may apply to the labor dispute arbitration committee for arbitration. Either party may also directly apply to the labor dispute arbitration committee for arbitration. If a party refuses to accept the arbitration award, that party may bring a lawsuit to the People's Court.

Article 80 A labor dispute mediation committee may be established within an employing unit. The labor dispute mediation committee shall be composed of representatives of the workers, representatives of the employing unit, and representatives of the trade union. The chairperson of the labor dispute mediation committee shall be held by a trade union representative.
Where a labor dispute is settled through mediation and an agreement is reached, the parties shall fulfill the agreement.

Article 81 A labor dispute arbitration commission shall be composed of representatives of the labor administrative department, representatives of the trade union at the same level, and representatives of the employing units. The director of the labor dispute arbitration commission shall be held by a representative of the labor administrative department.

Article 82 A party that raises an arbitration claim shall submit a written application to the labor dispute arbitration commission within sixty days from the date on which the labor dispute arises. An arbitration award shall generally be made within sixty days from the date of receipt of the arbitration application. Where there is no objection to the arbitration award, the parties must comply with it.

Article 83 If a party to a labor dispute refuses to accept the arbitration award, it may institute proceedings in a People's Court within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the arbitration award. If a party neither institutes proceedings nor complies with the arbitration award within the statutory time limit, the other party may apply to a People's Court for compulsory execution.

Article 84 Where a dispute arises over the conclusion of a collective contract and the parties fail to resolve it through consultation, the labor administrative department of the local people's government may organize the relevant parties to coordinate and handle the matter.
Where a dispute arises over the performance of a collective contract and the parties fail to resolve it through consultation, they may apply to a labor dispute arbitration commission for arbitration; if they refuse to accept the arbitration award, they may institute proceedings in a People's Court within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the arbitration award.

Article 85 The labor administrative departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall, according to law, supervise and inspect the compliance of employing units with labor laws and regulations, have the power to stop any act that violates labor laws and regulations, and order rectification.

Article 86 When performing their official duties, the supervision and inspection personnel of the labor administrative departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall have the right to enter the employing units to inquire into the implementation of labor laws and regulations, review necessary materials, and inspect the workplaces.
When performing their official duties, the supervision and inspection personnel of the labor administrative departments of the people's governments at or above the county level must present their credentials, enforce the law impartially, and comply with the relevant provisions.

Article 87 The relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall, within their respective functions and duties, supervise the compliance of employing units with labor laws and regulations.

Article 88 Trade unions at all levels shall, according to law, safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of workers, and supervise the compliance of employing units with labor laws and regulations.
Any organization or individual shall have the right to report and accuse any act that violates labor laws and regulations.

Article 89 Where the labor rules and regulations formulated by an employing unit violate the provisions of laws or regulations, the labor administrative department shall give a warning, order rectification; if damage is caused to workers, the employing unit shall bear compensation liability.

Article 90 Where an employing unit, in violation of the provisions of this Law, extends the working hours of workers, the labor administrative department shall give a warning, order rectification, and may impose a fine.

Article 92 Where the labor safety facilities and labor hygiene conditions of an employing unit do not meet the national standards or it fails to provide workers with necessary labor protection articles and labor protection facilities, the labor administrative department or the relevant department shall order rectification and may impose a fine; if the circumstances are serious, the matter shall be submitted to the people's government at or above the county level for a decision to order suspension of production for rectification; if no measures are taken against potential accident hazards, resulting in a major accident causing loss of life or property of workers, the persons responsible shall be investigated for criminal liability in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law.

Article 93 Where an employing unit compels workers to operate in violation of rules and at risk, resulting in a major accident involving casualties and causing serious consequences, the persons responsible shall be investigated for criminal liability according to law.

Article 94 Where an employing unit illegally recruits minors under the age of sixteen, the labor administrative department shall order rectification and impose a fine; if the circumstances are serious, the market supervision and administration department shall revoke its business license.

Article 95 Where an employing unit violates the provisions of this Law on the protection of female workers and underage workers and infringes upon their legitimate rights and interests, the labor administrative department shall order rectification and impose a fine; if damage is caused to female workers or underage workers, the employing unit shall bear compensation liability.
Article 97 Where a void contract entered into due to the reason of the employing unit causes damage to the worker, the employing unit shall bear compensation liability.

Article 98 Where an employing unit rescinds a labor contract in violation of the conditions provided for in this Law, or deliberately delays the conclusion of a labor contract, the labor administrative department shall order rectification; if damage is caused to the worker, the employing unit shall bear compensation liability.

Article 99 Where an employing unit recruits a worker whose labor contract has not yet been terminated, causing economic losses to the original employing unit, the said employing unit shall bear joint and several compensation liability according to law.

Article 100 Where an employing unit fails to pay social insurance premiums without justification, the labor administrative department shall order it to pay within a time limit; if it fails to pay within the time limit, a late fee may be imposed.

Article 101 Where an employing unit unreasonably obstructs the labor administrative department, the relevant departments, and their staff members from exercising their supervisory and inspection powers, or retaliates against informants, the labor administrative department or the relevant department shall impose a fine; if the act constitutes a crime, the person liable shall be investigated for criminal liability according to law.

Article 102 Where a worker rescinds the labor contract under conditions violating the provisions of this Law or violates the confidentiality matters agreed upon in the labor contract, thereby causing economic losses to the employing unit, the worker shall bear compensation liability according to law.

Article 103 Where a staff member of the labor administrative department or the relevant department abuses his power, neglects his duty, or engages in malpractice for personal gain, if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if it does not constitute a crime, an administrative sanction shall be imposed.

Article 104 Where a state functionary or a staff member of a social insurance fund management agency misappropriates social insurance funds, if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 105 Where the violation of the provisions of this Law infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of workers, and other laws or administrative regulations have already provided for penalties, the penalties shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of such laws or administrative regulations.

Article 106 The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, pursuant to this Law and the actual circumstances of their regions, prescribe the implementation procedures for the labor contract system and report them to the State Council for record.
Article 107 This Law shall come into force as of January 1, 1995.
